name: AR-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Well-funded incumbent Westerman vs. near-zero Democratic fundraising
No polls or expert ratings; fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: An R+20 incumbent district with a massively outspent, underfunded challenger leaves no evidence to move off the baseline; markets and fundamentals both point to a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or national wave could put this in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bruce Westerman, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a southern Arkansas district that leans about twenty points Republican. He has raised over $2.5 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic nominee James Russell has raised under six thousand dollars with almost nothing on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture.

Prediction markets give Westerman roughly a 97 percent chance of winning, consistent with the baseline model's expected margin near nineteen points. Barring an unforeseen shock, this seat is very likely to remain in Republican hands.
